meta.title: Terms of Use • CrookCatcher Android App
meta.description: Terms of use for CrookCatcher, the Android app that takes pictures when wrong passwords are entered.

hero.title: Terms of Use
hero.lead: By downloading and using CrookCatcher, you agree to the following terms and conditions. Please read them carefully.

You may not modify or copy the materials in this app or use them for any commercial purpose. Attempting to decompile or reverse engineer any software contained in the app is prohibited.

sections.title: Data and Ads
sections.body: CrookCatcher collects anonymous usage data and crash reports with Google Analytics and Firebase, such as when an email is sent and how you navigate through the app. You can opt out in the app settings. The free version of the app shows ads provided by Google AdMob. Your photos, videos and location are not shared with the developer. Please refer to our Privacy Policy for details.

sections.title: Paid plans and refunds
sections.body:
Some CrookCatcher features may be paid—a subscription or a one-time unlock. The company that actually charges you is whoever you checked out with: usually Google Play for purchases inside the Android app, or Paddle (or a similar partner) if you pay on the web. Their terms apply to that payment as well.

Subscriptions renew automatically until you cancel. If a free trial is offered, it turns into a paid subscription at the end unless you cancel before then. You can cancel at any time in Google Play (Payments & subscriptions, then Subscriptions) or with the company you paid, and you keep access until the end of the period you already paid for. A one-time unlock is a single payment with no further charges.

If you’d like a refund, how that works and how long you have depend on that same company. Please use their help center or refund flow first—that’s usually the quickest path. You can also contact CrookCatcher support with your receipt or order details; we’ll help however we can, but only the payment provider can approve or deny the refund.

After you already have access to what you bought, we don’t offer refunds on our own, except where Google Play, Paddle, or the law says otherwise, including any statutory rights you have as a consumer.
